record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.context_brief: Stability and strict feasibility of quasi-isometric minimizers
record.original_question: For the same quasi-isometric functional, can one characterize stability conditions for minimizers and prove, if true, that every minimizer remains strictly inside the feasible set, meaning that there is a positive margin epsilon and a parameter t1>t+epsilon such that det grad y - t1 Phi(det grad y, grad y) > 0 almost everywhere? Such a result would support the weak Euler-Lagrange formulation and possible higher regularity of grad y.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n=2$ or $3$) be a bounded reference domain, and consider deformations $y: \Omega 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ in a suitable Sobolev class (e.g. $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$) with prescribed boundary data. Fix a continuous function $\Phi:\mathbb{R}	imes\mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}	o(0,\infty)$ (a metric/weight function) and a real parameter $t>0$. Define the feasible set
$$\mathcal{F}_t = \{\,y : \det
abla y(x) - t\,\Phi(\det
abla y(x),
abla y(x)) > 0 	ext{ a.e. in }\Omega\,\},$$
and consider a quasi-isometric (barrier-type) functional $I_t[y]$ of polyconvex form whose finiteness is equivalent to $y\in\mathcal{F}_t$ and which penalizes deviation from isometry. Assume $I_t$ admits a minimizer $y^\star$ over admissible deformations with given Dirichlet data.

Problem. (a) Formulate and prove stability conditions for minimizers $y^\star$ of $I_t$ with respect to perturbations of the data (boundary values, parameter $t$, and weight $\Phi$). (b) Show that every such minimizer is strictly interior to the feasible set, i.e. there exist $\varepsilon>0$ and $t_1 > t+\varepsilon$ such that
$$\det
abla y^\star(x) - t_1\,\Phi(\det
abla y^\star(x),
abla y^\star(x)) > 0 \quad	ext{for a.e. }x\in\Omega.$$
Use this strict feasibility to justify the weak Euler–Lagrange equation for $I_t$ at $y^\star$ and to establish higher regularity of $
abla y^\star$.
artifact.status_search_result: Literature on barrier variational quasi-isometric grid generation describes the functional and its feasible set, but stability of minimizers and strict interior feasibility (with the resulting weak Euler–Lagrange formulation and higher regularity of the gradient) are listed among unsolved theoretical problems; no published proof of these properties was found.

status_evidence.title: Barrier variational generation of quasi-isometric grids
status_evidence.snippet: Grid generation method based on the minimization of the discrete barrier functional with feasible set consisting of quasi-isometric grids; deviation from isometry minimized via contraction of the feasible set.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the quasi-isometric barrier functional framework but does not establish strict interior feasibility or stability of continuous minimizers.

status_evidence.title: Grid generation and adaptation by functionals (SciELO)
status_evidence.snippet: Geometric interpretations of smoothness functionals and Euler–Lagrange equations used in adaptive grid construction.
status_evidence.claim: Discusses Euler–Lagrange equations for grid functionals without resolving strict feasibility/regularity of minimizers.
